header.running_head: Exercising Patience upon Misfortunes in General

blocks.text: The statement of Hadhrat Umar (RA) that everything which Affects a Mu'min is a Calamity if he does not Like it

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Khalifah narrates that he was once with Hadhrat Umar (RA) when the strap of his sandal broke. Hadhrat Umar (RA) recited:
"إِنَّا لِلّٰهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُوْنَ"
"To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return"
Thereafter (to explain why he said this), Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Everything that is unpleasant to you is regarded as a calamity."[^1]

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when the front portion of Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s shoe broke, he exclaimed:
"إِنَّا لِلّٰهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُوْنَ"
"To Allaah we belong and to Him shall we return"
"O Ameerul Mu'mineen!" the people enquired, "You are reciting () for a mere front portion of a shoe?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "When anything that he finds unpleasant happens to a Mu'min, it is regarded as a calamity."[^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Commands Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) to Persevere Against the Enemy and The Perseverance of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) until he was Martyred

Hadhrat Aslam reports that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) once wrote to Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), informing him that the Romans were launching a massive military offensive and also stating the grave dangers they (the Muslim army) faced. In his reply after duly praising Allaah, Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote, "Whenever any difficulty afflicts a Mu'min, Allaah creates ease afterwards and no difficulty can overpower two eases[^3]. Allaah states in His book:

blocks.arabic_text: يٰٓأَيُّهَا الَّذِيْنَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوْا وَصَابِرُوْا وَرَابِطُوْا وَاتَّقُوا اللّٰهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُوْنَ
blocks.text: O you who have Imaan! Exercise sabr, compete in patience, continue doing good deeds (especially ensuring that the borders of Muslim countries are well guarded) and fear Allaah so that you may be successful (in reaching your goal).[^4]
Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Mahdi says that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) possessed
Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd bin Humayd, Ibn Mundhir and Bayhaqi.
Marwazi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.154).
Here Hadhrat Umar (RA) was referring to the verses of the Qur'aan where Allaah states:, meaning that every difficulty is followed by two eases.
Maalik, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi Dunya, Ibn Jareer, Hakim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.154).
